source.title: Large Scale Foundation Model on Single-cell Transcriptomics
source.authors: Minsheng Hao; Jing Gong; Xin Zeng; Chiming Liu; Yu-Cheng Guo; Xingyi Cheng; Tai-Feng Wang; Jian-Zhu Ma; Xue-Gong Zhang; Leo T. Song

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies a scale sweep to a new setting—single-cell transcriptomics—and reports how its pretraining loss changes with model size and FLOPs.
record.gate_note: The authors’ background statement about language-model scaling is not a study result. Downstream task results are not linked to a sweep over scale or pretraining loss, so they do not test downstream predictability (V6).
record.test_reason: The study pretrains xTrimoGene models at 3M, 10M and 100M parameters on single-cell transcriptomics. It reports that validation loss falls as a power law in parameters and FLOPs (Fig. 2A). That is a result on the power-law form in a new modality, which bears on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say the LLM scaling law was also confirmed in their framework and that scFoundation scales effectively. They add that the 100M model achieved the lowest reconstruction loss among models sized like prior single-cell models.
record.recipe_differences: Tests a single-cell transcriptomics model with read-depth-aware regression loss, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy; the reported comparison uses three model sizes and does not report a compute-optimal allocation.
record.problems: Only three model sizes are reported; the text gives no numerical loss values or fitted exponents. The figure caption calls the measure training loss, whereas the text calls it validation loss.

untested.parts: Only single-cell transcriptomics with a regression (MSE) masked-value objective is tested. Image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer regimes are untested, as is scaling with data or tokens.
Language-model held-out loss is not studied.
No fits on small runs are used to predict much larger runs.
No allocation of parameters and tokens under a fixed compute budget.
No comparison of model shapes at fixed parameter count.
Downstream tasks are run only with the 100M model against baselines; there is no sweep over scale or loss.
No analysis of how fitting or setup choices affect exponents, and no curvature analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The DOI is the Nature Methods published version, but the text supplied is the June 2023 bioRxiv preprint, so 'preprint' describes the text read rather than the DOI. Most of the paper is downstream benchmarking of a single 100M model, which does not bear on the scaling versions.

versions.untested_parts: Tests neither language-model cross-entropy nor loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute in language models.
Does not test whether fits on smaller runs predict much larger runs.
Does not compare parameter/token allocations under a fixed compute budget.
Does not compare architecture details at fixed parameter count.

Tests a scaling trend only for single-cell transcriptomics models trained with read-depth-aware regression. It does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer as scaling regimes; the reported loss is not cross-entropy.
Does not test whether downstream performance varies predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
Does not test dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices, or whether curves bend away from a power law.

rows.subject: xTrimoGene architecture models
rows.operation_detail: Compared model sizes and training FLOPs during pretraining.
rows.measure: Validation loss; the pretraining objective is regression loss on masked gene-expression values, not cross-entropy.
rows.value: The validation loss exhibited a power-law decline as model parameters and total FLOPs increased.
rows.locator: Results, “scFoundation is a scalable model for read-depth enhancement without fine-tuning”; Fig. 2A
rows.note: The paper reports the trend collectively across three model sizes; it gives no numerical loss values in the text. Fig. 2A's caption calls the plotted quantity training loss, while the accompanying text describes loss on the validation dataset.
rows.check: The link and state stand, but the evidence is thin. It is a qualitative statement over three model sizes, with no loss values, fitted exponents or goodness of fit in the text. Whether data or steps were held fixed or bottlenecked is not stated. The Fig. 2A caption calls the measure training loss; the text says validation loss. The loss is MSE regression on masked expression values, not cross-entropy. The figure also shows dots for xTrimoGene models sized like previous models; these are not separately reported.

relationships.condition: xTrimoGene encoder-decoder models (3M, 10M, 100M parameters) pretrained with read-depth-aware masked regression on ~50M human single-cell transcriptomes
relationships.reason: The authors state that validation loss shows a power-law decline with parameters and FLOPs (r1). The support is weak: three sizes, no reported exponents or values.
relationships.display_finding: Validation loss showed a reported power-law decline with parameters and FLOPs across the three tested model sizes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: xTrimoGene models at the three reported parameter sizes, in single-cell transcriptomics pretraining
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that validation loss declines as a power law with increasing parameters and FLOPs in this setting (r1). This supports the power-law form in this modality, without establishing the broader regimes or cross-entropy formulation in V5.
